assumptions: Q10-SM's exact constructor can be replayed on fresh engineering states without changing its frozen semantics.
Model weights, bounds, products, accumulators, and stored readouts use finite IEEE-754 binary32 wherever the production learner does; nonfinite values fail closed.
The production learner's exact operation order and fused-versus-unfused behavior are part of the observed object and may not be optimized by the diagnostic observer.
Ordered-binary32 ULP distance uses a frozen total ordering that distinguishes signs and signed zero; NaN and infinity are invalid.
A legal ULP move is an actual adjacent binary32 storage value, not addition of an estimated decimal epsilon.
Starting-state one-move effects are a local capacity diagnostic and may change after subsequent moves.
Relaxed SVD capacity neither proves nor disproves discrete repairability.
The finite beam search is a deterministic constructor, not a completeness proof; exhaustion does not establish impossibility.
Exact sequential readout equality is necessary but insufficient without every final geometry and integrity gate.
The 16-step final reserve, 16-step per-coordinate spend, 64-move budget, beam width 64, and branch width 64 are conservative engineering choices made without behavioral evidence.
The f64 cue, axis, and norm tolerances are engineering admission gates, not biological, behavioral, direction, or exchangeability thresholds.
An already-equal endpoint measures storage mismatch frequency but does not demonstrate a nontrivial repair.
Parent-constructor-ineligible events remain in total coverage and cannot be replaced; repair denominators are reported separately.
No qualification outcome may change seeds, budgets, tolerances, status rules, or future direction and behavior gates.
Future behavioral, direction-effect, exchangeability, hidden-learning-state, future-plasticity, and metaplasticity claims remain unset.
claims_explicitly_forbidden: reinterpretation of Q09, Q10-BG, or Q10-SM
scientific exchangeability of true and repaired endpoints
